Home / The forest after dark

Puerto Nariño · Colombian Amazon

Rainforest night walk

A torchlight walk into a world of tiny creatures and extraordinary sounds.

Ask Amaru on WhatsApp ↗

About this experience

Discover another side of the rainforest on a guided walk after sunset. Move slowly by torchlight, listen to the forest and look for frogs, insects and other nocturnal life. This is a night walk, distinct from both daytime Kaya and an overnight forest stay; animal encounters cannot be guaranteed.

After dark, listening becomes a different way to discover the Amazon rainforest. With fewer distant views, attention shifts to nearby sounds, leaves and the small details picked out by a light. Night walks are among the nature activities described for this part of the Colombian Amazon; Amaru’s outing keeps that focus on careful observation with a guide.

Choose this experience for the atmosphere of the forest after sunset and the chance to look more closely. Go at the pace indicated by your guide and leave wildlife undisturbed. The walk is a separate experience from an overnight stay, so discuss those two interests independently when planning your visit.

Destination context sources: Parques Nacionales ↗

What to explore

  • A guided walk after dark
  • Nocturnal wildlife and forest sounds
  • Footwear, torch and route confirmed together

Before you go

Time of day
AFTER DARK
Duration
Confirm the duration and meeting point with Amaru for your dates.

Consider footwear with good grip, clothes covering arms and legs, and rain protection. Ask whether to bring a personal torch and whether boots or lighting are provided. Before confirming, discuss the terrain, difficulty, return arrangements and suitability for everyone in your group. Leave any equipment expectations until Amaru has clarified the proposal.

What should I confirm?

Ask about the route, departure, group requirements, guide language, equipment, transport and what is included. Share your dates and number of travellers, and review the full price and cancellation conditions before confirming anything.

Routes depend on water levels, weather and local conditions. Wildlife sightings cannot be guaranteed.
